\title{What the Commission's Conditions Actually Say:\\
\large a census of condition text, and the object it describes}
\author{Dan Post}
\date{September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
The conditions memo established that the Commission's conditions of approval live in its
motions, not in its minutes, and probed \ccOldPerYear\ cases a year for them against one URL
pattern per host. This memo replaces that sample with a census --- every case and every motion number
the item table records, probed against every place the department has published a motion ---
and then reads what the conditions say, before any coding scheme is imposed on them.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{Condition text reaches back further than the conditions memo said, but not far.} The
probe answered \ccProbed\ candidate URLs and found \ccProbeHits\ documents. Parsed
condition text now exists for \ccCondWithText\ of the \ccCondItems\ items the item table flags
as conditioned (\ccCondWithTextPct\%); the earliest of those items was heard in
\ccEarliestItemYear, and the oldest motion read dates from \ccEarliestAny. The conditions memo
put the boundary at 2010; the sources
that reach before it are the old site's document modules and FTP tree, the pre-2003 city pages
kept by the Wayback Machine, and adopted motions attached to later packets. They reach \ccReachEarlyHtml\% of conditioned items
heard in 1998--2002 and \ccReachLateHtml\% in 2003--2009, against \ccReachEarlyPdf\% in
2011--2014. The pre-2010 residual is overwhelmingly items for which no document was found at
any address: \ccResPreTenNone\ of \ccResPreTen.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{The conditions are a template with a thin project-specific layer.} \ccHeadingsDistinct\
distinct condition headings occur across the motions read; the \ccTopHeadings\ most frequent
carry \ccHeadingsTopShare\% of all headed conditions, and \ccHeadingsOnce\ occur in one motion
only. What varies from project to project is numbers --- hours, feet, periods, unit counts ---
and a short tail of conditions written for the site.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{The entitlement's maturity is written into the template.} The validity condition
states a period on \ccValidityStatePct\% of the motions that carry one, and on
\ccValidityModalShare\% of those the period is \ccValidityModal\ months. The extension
condition states a period on only \ccExtensionWithPeriod\ of the \ccExtensionN\ motions that
carry one: it extends the clock by the length of a delay caused by an agency, an appeal or a
lawsuit.
\end{abstract}

\section{Coverage: a census, replacing the conditions memo's sample}
\label{sec:coverage}

\paragraph{The universe.} A case is a distinct case number after upper-casing, stripping
white space and expanding a two-digit year against the hearing year; the function that says so
(\texttt{case\_universe} in \texttt{acquire\_external\_data.py}) is the one every memo now
imports. The item table holds \ccUniverse\ such cases. The corpus and conditions memos counted
\ccCasesPrinted, because they counted printed strings, and \ccCaseMerges\ cases were printed
both ways --- \texttt{99.530C} at one hearing and \texttt{1999.530C} at another. The census
probes the \ccUniverse, and every case count below is on that basis.

\subsection{What was searched}

The conditions memo's Table~4 asked whether a packet existed for \ccOldPerYear\ sampled cases
a year at two constructed addresses (\ccOldProbed\ cases, \ccOldFound\ packets found). Four things found while building the census changed the search,
and each became a stage of it.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{No directory lists its contents.} \ccListingsIndex\ of the \ccListingsTried\
directory and bucket-listing URLs tried returned an index, so every document has to be asked
for by name.
\item \textbf{The minutes link their own documents.} The HTML minutes hyperlink motions and
packets on the old \texttt{sf-planning.org} tree (the links run from \ccHtmlLinksFrom\ to
\ccHtmlLinksTo), and from \ccVaultLinksFrom\ the PDF minutes link every motion, resolution
and DRA number to the adopted document in the department's vault. Reading the raw corpus locally gave \ccMinutesLinks\ links from \ccMinutesLinkDocs\
minutes documents. Many of the archived HTML pages disable their links by renaming the
attribute to \texttt{data-href}; reading \texttt{href} alone had silently dropped every one.
\item \textbf{The archived agendas link the packets.} A crawl of \ccOldsitePages\ archived
agenda pages of the old site found \ccOldsiteLinks\ document links, and the 2015--2026 hearing
pages (\ccHearingPages\ of them) \ccHearingDocs\ more.
\item \textbf{The Wayback Machine holds the pre-2003 city site.} The CDX index returned
\ccCdxOk\ URLs captured with status 200 under the \ccCdxPrefixes\ prefixes searched
(Table~\ref{tab:cdx}). Almost all are agendas, notices and reports. The ones named by motion
or case are few: \ccCdxMotionsHtml\ HTML motion pages from the pre-2003 city site,
\ccCdxMotionsPdf\ motion PDFs and \ccCdxPackets\ packets, the motion captures from
\ccCdxFirstMotion\ and the packets from \ccCdxFirstPacket. That is the Wayback yield, reported
by year as the brief asks, and it is small.
\end{itemize}

Together the four sources gave \ccDiscoveredUrls\ distinct URLs, \ccDiscoveredCensus\ of them
about a case or a motion. The probe then asked for every case in the universe under every
case-keyed family --- as printed, as its stem, and as the stem with each suffix the minutes
attach to it --- and for every motion and resolution number under the motion families,
in the hearing year and the years either side. Table~\ref{tab:families} lists the families. It
used \texttt{HEAD}, falling back to a ranged \texttt{GET} where \texttt{HEAD} was refused, at
no more than \ccRatePerHost\ requests a second per host. It answered \ccProbed\ URLs: \ccProbeHits\
documents, \ccProbeMissing\ absent, \ccProbeLogin\ behind the vault's sign-in page or its
``not public'' error page, \ccProbeSoft\ redirected by a dead host to its new home page
(counted as absent, not as documents), and \ccProbeOther\ other.
The probe \ccProbeFinished.

\cctable{families}
\cctable{cdx}

Table~\ref{tab:negatives} records the searches that came back empty or closed, so that
nobody runs them again.

\cctable{negatives}

\subsection{The census}

Table~\ref{tab:census} is the census, by the first hearing year of the case or motion each
document belongs to and by URL family; Figure~\ref{fig:coverage} shows what it yielded, year by
year --- the motions read and the share of the conditioned docket they reach. The census is
what the conditions memo's Table~4 becomes when every case is asked about, and it replaces it.
Each family answers for its own span of years: the old site's document modules and FTP tree
for the last years of the HTML minutes, the motion archive for the first PDF years, the vault
from the first minutes that link it, the date-keyed packet host for the most recent hearings,
and the main packet host across most of the PDF era beside them. A case first heard early can
still have a packet if it came back to the Commission later, which is why the packet columns
reach back before the host existed. For cases first heard before the old site's span almost
nothing answers at a live address: the pre-2003 motions survive only as Wayback captures and
as exhibits to later packets.

\subsection{What was read, and the earliest year by source}

A document found is not a result; a document read is. Table~\ref{tab:coverage} counts motion
sections with at least one parsed condition, one copy of each motion whichever address reached
it --- the same adopted motion arrives as a standalone file, a mirror copy and an exhibit to a
later packet --- by source and era. \textbf{The answer to the question the census was built for
is its last column}: the earliest hearing year for which condition text is retrievable, by
source.

\begin{itemize}
\item Adopted motions: the old site's FTP tree from \ccEarliestFtp, its document modules from
\ccEarliestModules, the department's vault from \ccEarliestVault, and the pre-2003 city pages
(through the Wayback Machine) from \ccEarliestWayback.
\item Draft motions in packets: from \ccEarliestPackets.
\item Adopted motions embedded in later packets: from \ccEarliestEmbedded. A motion that
modifies an earlier approval attaches the original, so an old motion survives inside a new
packet. The oldest of these predate the corpus and belong to no case in it: \ccSectionsOutsideUniverse\
motion sections read belong to no case in the universe at all. The earliest motion read for a
case in the universe was heard in \ccEarliestInUniverse. Measured on the item table instead, the
earliest conditioned item that now has condition text was heard in \ccEarliestItemYear.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Correction (2026-09-11).} The previous version said that ``the earliest motion read
for a case in the universe was heard in \ccRprevEarliestInUniverse, years before the case came
back to the Commission''. No such motion was read. The document is the packet for case
\texttt{\ccFixPacketCase}, with two earlier adopted motions bound into it: Motion
\ccFixOldMotion\ of \ccFixOldDate\ (case \texttt{\ccFixOldCase}), and Motion \ccFixNewMotion\ of
\ccFixNewDate\ (case \texttt{\ccFixNewCase}), a restaurant next door. The older motion is a scan
whose running header repeats ``CITY PLANNING COMMISSION / MOTION NO.'' on every page, so every
page read as a title page, and the rule that folds a title block spilling onto a second page
into one section folded the later motion into the older one: its conditions were filed under
the older motion's date and, because the later case number is printed on more pages, under the
later case. The parser now opens a new section at a title page that carries a different motion
number (round~3, \S\ref{sec:validation}). Every year-span that rested on it moves:
Tables~\ref{tab:sections} and~\ref{tab:headings} no longer begin at
\ccRprevEarliestInUniverse, and the earliest motion read for a case in the universe is now
\ccEarliestInUniverse.

\cctable{coverage}

\paragraph{How much of the conditioned docket has text.} Table~\ref{tab:reach} crosses the
parsed sections with the item table. \ccCondWithText\ of the \ccCondItems\ conditioned items
(\ccCondWithTextPct\%) now have some condition text, draft or adopted --- \ccReachEarlyHtml\% of
those heard in 1998--2002, \ccReachLateHtml\% in 2003--2009, \ccReachTwentyTen\% in 2010,
\ccReachEarlyPdf\% in 2011--2014, \ccReachMidPdf\% in 2015--2017, \ccReachVault\% in 2018--2021
and \ccReachRecent\% in 2022--2026.

\cctable{reach}

\paragraph{The residual, named.} Table~\ref{tab:residual} sorts the \ccCondNoText\ conditioned
items without text by why. For \ccResFoundRead\ a document keyed to the item was found and read
and yielded no conditions --- a staff report, a Discretionary Review Action, a motion that
attaches none. For \ccResFoundUnread\ a document was found and not read: over the size cap,
a failed download, or a DRA, which the census counts and does not pull. For \ccResNoneNumber\
the item records a motion number and no document answered at any address; for
\ccResNoneNoNumber\ it records none, so only the case-keyed families could find it. Before
2010 the residual is almost entirely the last two kinds: \ccResPreTenNone\ of the
\ccResPreTen\ pre-2010 conditioned items without text had no document at any address. More
work on the parser will not move them; a records request might.

\cctable{residual}

\paragraph{Mention rate beside parse rate.} A change of format looks like missing data unless
the rate at which the documents \emph{mention} the thing is measured beside the rate at which
it is \emph{parsed}. Table~\ref{tab:mention} does that over the \ccSecRead\ motion sections
read. \ccSecMention\ mention an Exhibit A; \ccSecLocated\ have one located and parsed (a
located Exhibit A yields at least one parsed condition in all but \ccSecLocatedNone\ of them,
which is why the table carries one column for the two), and
\ccSecRejected\ have an ``Exhibit A'' that is some other attachment --- a draft ordinance, a
development agreement, the department's response to a CEQA appeal, a mitigation-monitoring
table --- which the parser now recognises and declines. The remaining \ccSecMentionNotLocated\
mention an Exhibit A that was neither located nor rejected. Reading a sample of them finds
three kinds: sections that mention another document's Exhibit A in running text (the ordinance,
agreement or mitigation program a resolution adopts), files that end before their Exhibit A,
and parser misses. The validation below is what measures the last.

\cctable{mention}

\subsection{How well the text is read}
\label{sec:validation}

The parsing rules live in \texttt{condition\_parser.py}, apart from the orchestration, so they
could be hashed and frozen. \ccGoldN\ documents spanning the eras and formats were drawn once,
with a fixed seed, stratified on era and container, and including documents with no conditions,
so that a detector finding conditions where there are none would show. The rules were frozen
(\ccValRoneFrozen) \emph{before} any label was written, and the documents were then labelled
condition by condition from the source layout, by readers who never saw the parser's output:
\ccValGoldConds\ conditions, after \ccValAdjudicated\ label was changed on checking the source
(a compliance line the source had numbered as if it were a condition; the decision is kept in
\texttt{gold\_adjudications.csv}).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Round 1, the rules as first frozen:} the parser's rows matched the labelled
boundaries with a precision of \ccValRoneInPrec\% and a recall of \ccValRoneInRecall\%. The
misses were systematic, not scattered: numbers printed as separate text objects beside their
lines, nested numbering in the 1998--2010 motions (lettered parts holding parenthesised
conditions), numbering that restarts or jumps, compliance lines that begin mid-line, and page
headers that scanned and HTML copies keep inside the text.
\item \textbf{Round 2:} each of those was fixed and the rules frozen again (\ccValRtwoFrozen). On
the same documents the precision was \ccValRtwoInPrec\% and the recall \ccValRtwoInRecall\%
(in-sample). Out of sample, \ccValRtwoOutRows\ canonical rows drawn at random after that freeze,
from documents pulled after it, were checked against the source pages: \ccValRtwoOutCorrect\ of
\ccValRtwoOutRows\ started and ended where the condition does.
\item \textbf{Round 3, the rules as used:} this memo's own tables showed round 2 running one
condition into the next --- ``Sidewalk Maintenance'' holding ``10.~Community Liaison'', a
``Conformity with Current Law'' that stated ``60 percent'', a ``Lighting'' condition that stated
a period of ``107 years'' (the age of a cottage, in a neighbour's letter bound after the draft
motion), and the \ccRprevEarliestInUniverse\ date corrected above. The round-2 checks had not caught it because a
section read as one block is one row however many conditions it holds, and a row drawn at
random rarely lands on it. Six boundary rules were added, each written against a failure a
corpus-wide detector found, never against the gold labels (the gold documents were not opened):
a title page with a different motion number opens a new section; a letter ends an Exhibit A;
a numbered list inside one condition (the transformer-vault schedule) no longer makes the
2011--2014 bold-named template ``numbered''; the numbering margin follows the page on a
shifted scan; in a numbered section, prose opening with a name after a closed compliance line
is a condition whose number the scan lost; and a garbled footer is not a section head.
Table~\ref{tab:roundeffect} counts what they changed over the whole parse. The rules were
frozen again (\ccValFrozen). On the gold documents the precision is \ccValInPrec\% and the
recall \ccValInRecall\%; the heading matches the label on \ccValInHead\% of the \ccValInHeadN\
matched rows that carry one, and in the \ccValNoneDocs\ gold documents with no conditions the
parser found \ccValNoneFalse. \textbf{These are in-sample figures}: the gold documents belong to
the pool the rules were written against. Of the \ccValCarryRows\ rows round~2 was checked on
out of sample, round~3 reproduces \ccValCarryReproduced\ exactly, \ccValCarryCorrect\ of them
correct: round~2's out-of-sample figure stands for round~3 on those rows.
\item \textbf{Out of sample, round 3:} \ccValOutRows\ canonical rows drawn at random, after the
third freeze, from \ccValOutDocs\ documents outside the gold set that were pulled after it ---
documents no rule was written against --- and checked against the source pages. \ccValOutPrec\%
start and end where the condition does (\ccValOutStart\% start correctly, \ccValOutEnd\% end
correctly), and the heading is right on \ccValOutHead\% of the \ccValOutHeadN\ that have one.
\textbf{These are the figures to quote}, with one qualification: the documents pulled after the
third freeze are the last of the pull --- the largest packets --- and the rows drawn from them
were all heard between \ccValOutYearFrom\ and \ccValOutYearTo, in the modern template, so this
sample says nothing about the older formats; for those, round~2's check, which round~3
reproduces row for row, is the out-of-sample evidence.
\end{itemize}

\cctable{roundeffect}

\section{Anatomy of one motion}
\label{sec:anatomy}

Table~\ref{tab:anatomy} walks one conditional-use motion end to end:
Motion~No.~\ccAnatMotion, case \texttt{\ccAnatCase}, adopted \ccAnatAdopted, \ccAnatPages\
pages (\href{\ccAnatUrl}{source}). It is chosen by rule rather than by taste --- the
born-digital adopted conditional-use motion in the modern template with the median number of
conditions --- so it is the typical case, not the interesting one.

The motion has two halves, and only the second is conditions. The first is the Commission's
reasoning: a title block, a preamble reciting the application and the environmental
determination, and findings. Two of the findings carry the discretion. Under Planning Code
\S303 the Commission finds that the use is necessary or desirable and compatible with the
neighbourhood; under \S101.1 it finds the project consistent with the priority policies.
The decision paragraph then approves the application subject to the conditions attached as
Exhibit A and in general conformance with the plans on file stamped Exhibit B, and the
Commission secretary certifies the vote.

The second half is Exhibit A. It opens with standing blocks that are not conditions of the
project but terms of the approval itself --- what is authorised, that the conditions are
recorded against the parcel, printed on the plans, severable, and how they may be changed ---
and then the numbered or named conditions, grouped under section heads. The plans, Exhibit B,
are cited and kept on file; they are not bound into the motion. That matters for what
follows: the building's shape is fixed by the plans, so a condition that changes it has to be
written out, and most do not.

\cctable{anatomy}

\section{Every standing section, and the most frequent headings}
\label{sec:template}

Table~\ref{tab:sections} lists the standing blocks and the section heads under which conditions
are grouped, each with the number of motion sections carrying it, the share of conditional-use
motions that carry it, the median length of a condition's body under it, and the first and
last hearing year it was seen. The \ccPreambleBlocks\ preamble blocks and the \emph{Performance} and
\emph{Monitoring} sections are on the large majority of conditional-use motions,
\emph{Operation} and \emph{Design} on most, and \emph{Parking and Traffic} and
\emph{Provisions} on a minority --- selected by project.
The 1998--2009 motions group their conditions differently --- ``General Conditions'', or
lettered parts such as ``The Approved Project'' and ``Operation'' with parenthesised
conditions under each --- and those appear as their own rows.

\cctable{sections}

Table~\ref{tab:headings} gives the \ccTopHeadings\ most frequent condition headings, with the
same statistics and three more: the share of the heading's bodies that are \emph{identical} to
its most common body once numbers are masked --- the part of the condition that never varies
---, the share stating a quantity with a unit, and the commonest quantities stated. Sorted by those
statistics, the headings fall into three kinds (a heading can fall in none).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{A fixed text, with at most a number changing} (template share at least
\ccKindBoilerMin\%; \ccKindBoilerN\ headings): \ccKindBoiler. Once the number is masked,
most bodies are word for word the template; what a project changes, where it changes anything,
is the figure.
\item \textbf{A varying text that states a quantity} (template share below
\ccKindBoilerMin\%, a quantity in at least \ccKindNumberMin\% of bodies; \ccKindNumberN):
\ccKindNumber. The figure is the point, and the sentence around it is rewritten to fit.
\item \textbf{A recurring heading over a project-written body} (template share below
\ccKindBespokeMax\%; \ccKindBespokeN): \ccKindBespoke. The name recurs; what it asks for is
written for the site.
\end{itemize}

What varies across projects, then, is hours, days, distances, counts of spaces and units, the
period of validity, and the text of a few site-specific conditions; what does not vary is the
enforcement and revocation apparatus and the clock. Table~\ref{tab:examples} quotes up to three
bodies for each block and heading --- the earliest, a typical one and the one least like the
rest --- each cut at \ccQuoteWords\ words, with the page of the source document and a link to
it. Identical bodies are not repeated, so a block with one example has only one form.

\cctable{headings}
\cctable{examples}

\paragraph{Wording drift.} Table~\ref{tab:drift} compares, for each frequent heading with enough
bodies in two or more eras, the most common body in the first era it appears and in the last,
on number-masked text. Of the \ccDriftN\ headings compared, \ccDriftSame\ kept the same
most common sentence from the first era to the last (a similarity of at least
\ccDriftSameMin).
\ccDriftRewrittenN\ were rewritten --- a similarity below \ccDriftRewriteMax\ --- and they are
the rows at the top of the table: \ccDriftRewritten. For most of them the lowest similarity
between adjacent eras is as low as that between the first era and the last: the sentence was
replaced at one step rather than drifting.

\section{The long tail}
\label{sec:tail}

\ccHeadingsOnce\ of the \ccHeadingsDistinct\ distinct headings occur in one motion only.
Table~\ref{tab:tail} quotes \ccTailN\ of those conditions, drawn at random with a fixed seed, with
the kind of case each belongs to. These are the conditions a coding scheme will not anticipate,
and they are where the Commission's attention to the particular site shows. A count of them
per motion would be a cleaner measure of bespoke conditioning than the total. The draw is from
headings seen once, so a condition whose heading is common but whose body is not is not in it;
some drawn rows are also parser artefacts (a heading read from the first words of a sentence),
which is what a random draw of one-offs is expected to surface.

\cctable{tail}

\section{Counts as a variable}
\label{sec:counts}

A motion's condition count is the simplest measure of stringency the census makes available,
and nothing in the item table can compute it. Table~\ref{tab:peryear} and
Figure~\ref{fig:counts} give it by hearing year for adopted motions (numbered or named
conditions only; the \ccPreambleBlocks\ preamble blocks are excluded because every modern motion
has them),
beside the share of items the item table flags as conditioned. The median adopted motion
carries \ccPerMotionMedian\ conditions (mean \ccPerMotionMean). Across the \ccPerMotionYears\
years with at least \ccMinMotionsYear\ motions read, the rank correlation between the median
count and the conditioning share is \ccPerMotionRho: \textbf{the count \ccCountVerdict\ the
conditioning share.} Read with the corpus memo's substitution --- denial falling, conditioning
rising --- that says the rise is in how often the Commission conditions, more than in how much
each approval carries.

\section{Draft against adopted}
\label{sec:diff}

The packet carries the draft motion; the Commission adopts a motion that may differ. Where the
census has both for a case --- the latest draft heard on or before the adoption, and the
adopted motion --- Table~\ref{tab:diff} matches their conditions: by heading where both carry
headings, allowing for OCR in the adopted copy, and then what is left by number-masked text
(in \ccDiffByText\ pairs the drafts carry no headings and text is the only key). The adopted
copy is often a signed scan read by OCR, so a condition whose text differs by a misread letter
or a touched-up word is \emph{near-identical}, not changed; only a condition less than
\ccDiffSame\% similar to the draft's counts as reworded. Of \ccDiffPairs\ pairs,
\ccDiffAnyChange\ (\ccDiffAnyChangePct\%) differ in some condition. Of the \ccDiffDraftConds\
conditions in the drafts, \ccDiffIdentical\ are carried word for word and \ccDiffNear\
near-identical --- \ccDiffCarriedPct\% in all --- \ccDiffChanged\ are reworded and
\ccDiffRemoved\ dropped, and the adopted motions carry \ccDiffAdded\ conditions the drafts did
not.

\paragraph{What the additions are.} A condition the adopted motion carries and the draft does
not is not necessarily one the Commission added from the dais. Many are the template's standing
conditions --- Revocation, Noise Control, Managing Traffic During Construction, an odor-control
unit, an area-plan fee --- which are more plausibly staff completing the draft between the packet
and adoption, or conditions the parse missed on the draft side, than Commission action. The
table therefore splits them: an addition is \emph{template text} when its opening
\ccDiffTemplateChars\ characters, numbers masked, recur in the motions of at least
\ccDiffTemplateCases\ other cases. \ccDiffAddedTemplate\ of the \ccDiffAdded\ additions are
template text and \ccDiffAddedOther\ are not. Table~\ref{tab:added} quotes a random draw of the
latter; even those mix the Commission's changes with staff's, and nothing in the documents says
which is which.

The lower panel crosses the change with the item table's record of the hearing. The item
table records modifications for \ccDiffMods\ of the pairs, and in \ccDiffModsChange\ of those
the conditions did change. It records none for \ccDiffNoModsChange\ pairs whose conditions
changed nonetheless --- \ccDiffNoModsBeyond\ of them with a change beyond template additions
(a condition reworded or dropped, or a non-template one added). \textbf{The draft is a good
proxy for most of the adopted text.} What the comparison does not establish is that the
\texttt{modifications} field misses the Commission's own changes: the changes it does not record
are partly the Commission's and partly staff completing the draft, and the documents cannot
separate the two.

\cctable{diff}
\cctable{added}

\section{The conditions that set the clock}
\label{sec:option}

Four conditions define the entitlement's maturity in the real-options frame: \emph{Validity}
(how long the approval lasts before a permit must issue), \emph{Diligent Pursuit} (that
construction, once permitted, continue), \emph{Expiration and Renewal} (what happens when the
permit lapses), and \emph{Extension} (when the clock stops). Table~\ref{tab:option} classes
each condition by its heading --- or, in the eras that print none, by the first words of its
body --- reads the first period its body states, and tabulates the periods by hearing year;
Figure~\ref{fig:validity} shows the validity period year by year.

The result is simple. The validity condition states a period on \ccValidityStatePct\% of the \ccValidityN\
motions that carry one, and the period is \ccValidityModal\ months on \ccValidityModalShare\%
of those; the exceptions are shorter or longer periods set for particular projects. Diligent
pursuit and expiration state the same period (Table~\ref{tab:option}). The extension condition carries no
period at all on most motions: of \ccExtensionN\ carrying one, \ccExtensionWithPeriod\ state
a period. The modern text reads ``All time limits in the preceding three paragraphs may be
extended at the discretion of the Zoning Administrator where implementation of the project is
delayed by a public agency, an appeal or a legal challenge and only by the length of time for
which such public agency, appeal or challenge has caused delay.'' \textbf{The option's term is
fixed by template, and its extension is state-contingent}: it lengthens exactly when the
approval is litigated or held up by another agency.

\cctable{option}

\begin{figure}[htbp]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig_validity_period.pdf}
\caption{The period the validity condition gives the sponsor to obtain a permit, by hearing
year: the share of motions whose validity condition states fewer than, exactly, or more than
the modal \ccValidityModal\ months.}
\label{fig:validity}
\end{figure}

\section{The conditions memo's coding scheme on the full set}
\label{sec:taxonomy}

The conditions memo wrote a \ccTaxCategories-category keyword scheme against the headings of
the \ccOldFound\ packets its sample found. Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy} runs it unchanged on the census. By distinct heading it reaches
\ccTaxDistinct\% of the \ccTaxHeadings\ headings; weighted by how often each is imposed,
\ccTaxWeighted\%. On the eras that print no headings, where the scheme reads the body instead,
it reaches \ccTaxUnheaded\% of bodies --- a number that flatters it, because a body has more
words for a keyword to hit. Weighted by imposition, \ccTaxObligation\% of headed conditions
change the project's obligations and \ccTaxProject\% change the project. Table~\ref{tab:uncovered}
lists the most frequent headings the scheme misses, the first of them \ccUncoveredTop.

\textbf{The caveat stands.} The keywords were written by reading the conditions memo's packet
headings and revised once against the headings the first draft missed; the coverage figures
are in-sample to that extent. They support the claim that a small scheme spans most of what is
imposed, not that the scheme is a validated classifier.

\cctable{taxonomy}
\cctable{uncovered}

\section{The numbers inside the conditions}
\label{sec:numeric}

The template's words barely vary, and its figures do (\S\ref{sec:template}). So the figures are
read into typed columns rather than more prose parsed:
\texttt{conditions\_numeric.parquet} holds one row per canonical condition that states one of
them --- \ccNumConditions\ conditions --- with the motion section, case, hearing date and
heading, each typed value, and beside each value the words it was read from, so any value can be
checked against its sentence. Each field is read only from conditions of its own kind (by
heading, or the body's opening words where the era prints none), so a figure is never borrowed
from a neighbouring subject. The fields: the validity period in months; the first operating-hours
range a condition states (opening and closing hour, and whether it is daily, weekday or weekend);
bicycle parking spaces by class; the parking maximum; the inclusionary share, the dwelling and
affordable unit counts, and the income level the affordable-housing conditions state; screening
dimensions; notice radii and notice periods; and monitoring or reporting intervals. When the stage
was written \ccNumSpot\ values drawn at random across the fields were read against their
matched sentences and all were right; that is a check of the reading, not a validation of the
coverage, and no field has been checked for conditions it missed.

Table~\ref{tab:numeric} gives each field's distribution and Figure~\ref{fig:numeric} its
median and interquartile band by hearing year. Three things stand out. The validity period is
the template's (\ccNumValidity\ conditions state one; \S\ref{sec:option}). Operating hours are
set for the site: \ccNumHours\ conditions state a range, and \ccNumHoursLate\% of them let the
premises close after midnight. And the affordable-housing conditions state the inclusionary share
the project was held to --- \ccNumInclPct\ of them, from \ccNumInclPctFirst, most often
\ccNumInclPctMode\% --- which is the applied rate the exactions panel's vesting rule should
reproduce, an independent check on it. Screening dimensions are almost never stated
(\ccNumScreen\ conditions); the other screening conditions are the wireless template's, which
state none.

\cctable{numeric}

\label{fig:numeric}

\section{Recorded Notices of Special Restrictions}
\label{sec:nsr}

Every modern conditional-use motion carries a Recordation block requiring a Notice of Special
Restrictions to be recorded against the parcel, stating the conditions; the notices would reach
the conditions of cases whose motions are not online. Nothing was searched or downloaded to
check this; the Assessor-Recorder's public pages were read, and the terms below are quoted from
them (\href{https://www.sf.gov/get-copies-recorded-documents}{SF.gov, ``Get copies of recorded
documents''}; the official-records site's
\href{https://recorder.sfgov.org/html/DisclaimerContent.html}{disclaimer}). The index can be
searched ``by name, document number, document type, or by using the Assessor's Parcel Number''
and ``does not allow searches by property address''; ``online official record index information
is available from January 1, 1990 forward'', and ``documents recorded prior to January 1, 1990
can only be searched in our office''. A search returns an index entry. The image of a document
is available to registered users, whose registration asks for identity verification, and is
bought per document --- online at a per-document price plus a card fee, or in person at a
per-page price --- at the rates the SF.gov page lists. The disclaimer says nothing about
automated or bulk access, and the list of document types is not served to an anonymous
session, so whether ``Notice of Special Restrictions'' is a selectable type could not be
confirmed. \textbf{An index-only census of notices on the risk set's parcels is possible in
principle from 1990, one parcel at a time; the text costs a purchase per document; the
pre-1990 notices are in the office only; and whether bulk index access is permitted is a
question for the Recorder}, which this job did not ask.

\section{Established, and not established}

\textbf{Established.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item The case universe is \ccUniverse\ cases, defined once; the \ccCasesPrinted\ in the
earlier memos is printed strings, \ccCaseMerges\ of them the same case written two ways.
\item No directory lists the documents. The census found them by name: \ccProbeHits\ documents
among \ccProbed\ URLs asked for, from exact links in the minutes, the agenda and hearing pages
and the Wayback index, and from every case and motion number the item table records.
\item Condition text exists for \ccCondWithTextPct\% of conditioned items. It reaches back to
items heard in \ccEarliestItemYear, but before 2010 it is thin, and the pre-2010
residual is documents that were not found anywhere, not documents that were found and misread.
The conditions memo's ``no amount of work recovers condition content before 2010'' was a claim
about two URL patterns; the truth is ``little'', not ``none''.
\item The conditions are a template: a fixed apparatus of enforcement, revocation and clock, a
selected set of operating and design conditions whose text is fixed and whose numbers are the
project's, and a thin tail written for the site.
\item The count of conditions per motion is not rising with the conditioning share.
\item The option's term is fixed by template at \ccValidityModal\ months, and its extension is
contingent on delay by others.
\item The adopted conditions differ from the draft's in \ccDiffAnyChangePct\% of pairs, often
without the item table recording a modification; how much of that difference is the
Commission's rather than staff completing the draft is not established.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Not established.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item The residual. The motions for most pre-2010 conditioned items are not online; whether the
department holds them, and in what form, is a question for the department.
\item The recorded notices, which would reach the same cases from the other side; see
\S\ref{sec:nsr}.
\item A validated classifier. The scheme's coverage is in-sample; the next step is a
hand-coded set of conditions scored the way every other field is.
\item Whether the long tail predicts outcomes. It is quoted here, not yet coded.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Reproducing this}

\texttt{code/commission\_minutes\_processing/collect\_conditions.py} runs the census in stages,
each cached and resumable; the parsing rules are in \texttt{condition\_parser.py}.

{\small
\begin{verbatim}
python acquire_external_data.py sync     # materialise the Dropbox store
python collect_conditions.py discover    # listings, CDX, hearing and
                                         #   agenda pages, minutes' links
python collect_conditions.py probe       # HEAD every candidate
python collect_conditions.py pull --host <host> --loop-minutes 15 \
       --max-mb 60                       # one process per host
python collect_conditions.py reextract --network
                                         # pages read before /Rotate fix
python collect_conditions.py parse       # one row per condition
python collect_conditions.py diff        # draft against adopted
python collect_conditions.py gold        # draw the gold set (once)
python collect_conditions.py freeze --round 1   # hash the rules
python collect_conditions.py score --round 1    # against gold_labels
python collect_conditions.py archive --round 1  # keep round 1
python collect_conditions.py freeze --round 2   # after revising
python collect_conditions.py score --round 2    # in-sample
python collect_conditions.py sample --round 2   # rows after the
                                         #   freeze (once), checked by hand
python collect_conditions.py score --round 2    # ...and out of sample
python collect_conditions.py archive --round 2  # keep round 2, whole
                                         #   parse included
python collect_conditions.py freeze --round 3   # after the merge fixes
python collect_conditions.py parse
python collect_conditions.py score --round 3    # in-sample, and
                                         #   round 2's rows carried
python collect_conditions.py pull --host <host> --max-mb 2000
                                         # the rest of the pull
python collect_conditions.py parse
python collect_conditions.py sample --round 3   # out of sample (once)
python collect_conditions.py score --round 3
python collect_conditions.py summary     # task1_summary.md
python collect_conditions.py numbers     # conditions_numeric.parquet
python collect_conditions.py report      # tables, figures, macros
\end{verbatim}}

Everything lands in \texttt{\$MFHR\_DATA\_ROOT/external/cpc\_packets/}:
\texttt{manifests/} (discovery), \texttt{availability\_full.csv} (the census),
\texttt{docs/} (the motion sections kept, with their extracted lines), \texttt{pull\_log.csv}
(per-document wall time), \texttt{conditions\_long.parquet} (and \texttt{.csv}) and
\texttt{motion\_sections.csv} (the parse), \texttt{validation/} (the frozen round) and
\texttt{task1\_summary.md}. \texttt{report} regenerates
\texttt{tables/conditions\_content\_tables.tex}, \texttt{tables/conditions\_content\_macros.tex}
and the three figures. No number in
this memo is hand-placed.

\appendix
\section{Data dictionary for \texttt{conditions\_long}}
\label{sec:dictionary}

One row per condition: per (document, motion section, condition). Rows marked
\texttt{canonical} are the one copy of each motion section the analysis uses; the rest are the
same motion read from a mirror or an exhibit, kept so the choice can be audited.
